text:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: Increased 5xx and routing errors for /v1/generate in eu-west-1. Spike started ~3412109800. Auto-escalation: paging oncall.

pagerduty: @sam_w is paged (severity: sev2)

sam_w: on it. jumping in. seeing a big uptick in fallback rate from gen-v2 -> chat-instruct-v1.

maria_g: wait — why would gen requests be routed to chat-instruct? routing policy should only fallback to variants with compatible interface.

sam_w: initial quick check: routing table shows a release anchor "release-2026-04-15" mapped to model alias `gen-v2-primary` but the alias currently points to `chat-instruct-v1` in eu-west-1 due to a failed canary from last night.

alex_t: that sounds like a stale release mapping got swapped during the partial roll. seeing the same in control-plane logs: `alias.resolve(release-2026-04-15) -> chat-instruct-v1` at 3412109720.

jessica: customer impact: internal monitoring shows ~12% of embed/gen calls returned instruct responses; external error rate for a handful of customers spiked. Support is already seeing tickets. @support-bot can you gather affected customers?

support-bot: Found 8 customers with >1% error rate in the last 10m: acme-corp, travelx, noteapp-inc. Producing CSV to S3: s3://redwood-incident-archives/3412109876-affected.csv

nate_r: how are requests falling back? is it region-level fallback or variant mismatch?

sam_w: the fallback policy is 'compatible-variant-first, then cross-interface-last'. But there was an override in the eu-west policy for release-anchors that allowed any alias-compatible fallback to reduce latency during canary. That override was too permissive.

maria_g: timeline: a partial canary rolled last night to remove a GPU-optimized kernel; that canary failed and the control-plane attempted to re-anchor traffic to a previously healthy variant. A subsequent config apply updated the alias but didn't verify runtime interface compatibility.

alex_t: reproducing locally: send gen request to alias `release-2026-04-15` -> gets routed to chat-instruct -> runtime rejects payload shape for streaming tokens -> returns 500. logs: ```[3412109821] RuntimeError: function-calling-schema-mismatch: expected 'messages' array for chat, got 'prompt' string for gen```

jessica: we need immediate mitigation: either 1) revert alias to prior gen variant, or 2) change fallback policy to block cross-interface fallbacks. Which is fastest?

sam_w: revert alias is fastest. staging shows alias rollback succeeds in <15s if control-plane is healthy. I'll coordinate with infra to run rollback.

maria_g: while sam does rollback, flip the fallback override to strict in eu-west to prevent any further cross-interface fallbacks. That change is low-risk and reversible.

sam_w: executing rollback now: ```rbctl alias set release-2026-04-15 gen-v2-primary --region eu-west-1 --force```

system: rbctl acknowledged, job id 0x7a3f.

sam_w: job completed, alias now points to gen-v2-primary. Verifying traffic.

alex_t: can see alias resolved to gen variant across control-plane caches. Observability: fallback rate dropped from 18% -> 1.2% in 45s.

jessica: support: start templated reply to affected customers. Note: some responses were instruct-style, recommend re-running requests. Add note about potential duplicates.

support-bot: Draft reply saved: s3://redwood-incident-archives/3412109876/support-drafts/reply.txt

maria_g: toggling eu-west fallback override to strict now: ```PATCH /config/regions/eu-west-1/fallback-override { allow_cross_interface: false }```
system: config apply accepted (change-id 0x8b9c).

nate_r: any lasting capacity issues? Could the rollback cause a spike in latency?

sam_w: gen-v2-primary has fewer instances in eu-west-1 than chat-instruct, but autoscaler is healthy. We'll watch latency and ramp capacity if needed. So far p50/p95 stable.

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager handoff in 30m. Current severity: sev2 -> impacting but mitigated.

jessica: customer impact summary for postmortem: 8 customers affected, max 14% error rate for those customers, window ~3412109800–3412109900 (~2 minutes). Some JSON schema mismatches surfaced. No data exfiltration.

maria_g: root cause hypothesis: control-plane alias update during a failed canary left release anchor pointing to an incompatible variant because validation didn't check model interface compatibility for anchor updates.

alex_t: proposed fixes: 1) reject alias/anchor updates when target variant interface != anchor interface unless a force flag is used and an admin approves; 2) add an automated preflight that runs a lightweight compatibility check (payload shape) before applying alias; 3) add an observability alert for cross-interface fallback spikes.

sam_w: I'll own the rollback and immediate config flips. @maria_g can you take lead on the validation + preflight proposal? jessica will draft the customer comms and support runbooks. alex to own the alerting rule. nate to follow-up on capacity docs for rollbacks.

jessica: creating incident slack channel and postmortem ticket. postmortem link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-3412109876

pagerduty: @maria_g will be oncall for follow-up; handoff to next oncall @alex_t in 30m.

sam_w: leaving note — watch for any late-arriving replays from queued requests; we've added a temporary suppressor for duplicate-retry flood.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated at 3412110000. next steps: postmortem owner assigned, follow-up actions queued.

jessica: thanks team. I'll escalate to account execs for the top-3 affected customers and coordinate any SLA credits if necessary.

maria_g: will open a PR for alias validation and compatibility preflight today; marking as P0.

alex_t: logging final metrics snapshot to the incident archive. https://internal.metrics/3412109876/snapshot

nate_r: noted. I'll monitor autoscaler in next 2 hours and confirm no regressions.

support-bot: Notifying affected customers now. Templates sent.

sam_w: wrapping up oncall notes. handoff complete.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED (active mitigation complete).
